name: AL-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+23 partisan lean makes this one of the most Republican House seats
Rogers holds a roughly 40-to-1 fundraising advantage over McInnis ($2.5M vs $63K raised)
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 1%
No public polls or expert ratings; challenger lacks resources to alter fundamentals
model.rationale: The seat's deep Republican lean, Rogers' overwhelming financial edge, and market pricing near 99% Republican leave McInnis without a realistic path, so the forecast rests firmly on the fundamentals.
model.watch: A dramatic national Democratic wave or a major scandal involving Rogers could tighten the race, though the district's lean would still favor him heavily.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 3rd District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the House, with a partisan lean of roughly 23 points toward the GOP. Mike Rogers, the incumbent since 2003, is running for another term and holds an enormous financial advantage, having raised about $2.5 million and reporting $2.7 million on hand. Democratic challenger Lee McInnis has raised roughly $63,000, leaving little capacity to introduce herself to voters or contest the district's fundamentals.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for the race, and prediction markets price Rogers' chances near 99 percent. The district's composition, the incumbent's resources, and the absence of visible Democratic investment all point in the same direction. Barring an extraordinary outside event, Rogers is positioned to win re-election comfortably in November.
